issues.t: Power relay assembly can overheat and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from under the rear seat, a hybrid warning light, the car stalling or not restarting, or a blown main fuse.
issues.why: The power relay assembly (the main high-voltage relay box under the rear seat) can develop poor internal connections that heat up. Hyundai recalled 2017-2018 Ioniq hybrids and 2018 plug-ins, then issued a new remedy in 2022 because the first fix was not enough.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check the VIN for open recalls even if the first recall was done; the newer campaign replaces the earlier fix.

issues.t: Hybrid clutch actuator oil leak can short out wiring (recall)
issues.sym: A Check Hybrid System warning, loss of drive power, the car limiting itself to low speed, or oil leaks.
issues.why: A seal in the hydraulic clutch actuator for the hybrid transmission can leak, letting oil collect where it can cause an electrical short and fire risk. Some owners say problems returned after the recall work.
issues.next: Confirm the recall was done. If the hybrid warning appears or the car loses power, have it towed to a Hyundai dealer.

issues.t: Coolant can reach the power control unit and stall the car (recall)
issues.sym: The car shuts down or stalls while driving, with warning lights.
issues.why: Manufacturing flaws in the electric power control unit on some 2017 Ioniq Electrics let coolant reach the circuit board.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Confirm with a Hyundai dealer that the recall was completed.

issues.t: Reduced power or creeping forward from a bad charger ground (recall)
issues.sym: The car suddenly enters a low-power mode, or keeps moving forward briefly after you lift off the accelerator.
issues.why: A poor electrical ground at the onboard charging module can upset the drive system, putting the car into fail-safe mode.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the VIN and perform the recall repair. Until then, be ready to brake firmly if the car behaves oddly.

issues.t: Rear lug nuts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: A clicking or clunking from a rear wheel, vibration, or in the worst case a wheel coming off.
issues.why: Right-side rear lug nuts on some cars were not tightened enough at the factory.
issues.next: If you hear clicking from a wheel, stop and check the nuts. Have a dealer inspect and torque them under the recall.

issues.t: Car won't start or shuts down from a weak 12V battery
issues.sym: The car won't power on, locks itself, or the electrical system shuts down; the instrument cluster may go blank.
issues.why: The small 12-volt system can be drained by a fault or simply wear out. On the hybrid the 12V lithium battery is built into the hybrid battery pack and has a reset button on the dash; the Electric uses a conventional 12V battery.
issues.next: On the hybrid, press the 12V BATT RESET button. If it keeps happening, have the 12V battery tested and a drain test done.

issues.t: Jerky or hesitant low-speed shifts from the dual-clutch transmission
issues.sym: Lurching, jerking or hesitation when pulling away, at very low speed, or when the transmission downshifts during regenerative braking.
issues.why: The Ioniq hybrid and plug-in use a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic, which can engage roughly at low speed. Some owners also report a sudden jerk when releasing the brake in Drive.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check for software updates for the transmission and hybrid control unit. If the shifts are getting worse or come with a warning light, have it diagnosed.

issues.t: Check engine light from a tiny EVAP leak code
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0456, usually with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: Hyundai issued bulletins and a service campaign to add an air filter kit to the evaporative emissions system, which can falsely detect a small leak, especially in coastal areas.
issues.next: Make sure the fuel cap clicks shut. Ask a dealer whether the EVAP filter campaign applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Electronic parking brake and Auto Hold warnings
issues.sym: The EPB and Auto Hold lights come on with a chime, Auto Hold stops working, or the parking brake won't apply or release. The lights often clear after a restart and then return.
issues.why: Hyundai issued bulletins for parking brake motor fault codes C2416/C2417, including ones set by vibration. Causes include a software issue, wiring shorts and failing rear caliper motors.
issues.next: Use the regular brake firmly when stopped and do not rely on the parking brake until it is fixed. Ask a dealer about the parking brake software update and wiring checks.

issues.t: Clunk or rattle from the steering column
issues.sym: A knock, rattle or clunk felt in the steering wheel over bumps or when turning at low speed.
issues.why: The bearing for the worm shaft in the electric power steering column wears. Hyundai issued several bulletins to replace the worm shaft bearing or assembly.
issues.next: Have a dealer check for the steering column bulletins. It is mainly a noise problem but should be fixed.

issues.t: Braking feels uneven when switching from regenerative to friction brakes
issues.sym: Brake force changes without pedal input, the car lurches, or stopping power drops for a second, especially on wet roads when ABS engages.
issues.why: These cars blend regenerative braking with the normal hydraulic brakes. Owners report rough or incomplete handoffs between the two, and Hyundai issued a software update for brake pedal sensitivity on 2019 models.
issues.next: Have a dealer check for brake system software updates and inspect the brakes. Leave extra following distance until it is resolved.

issues.t: Hybrid warning lights from motor or control unit faults
issues.sym: A hybrid system or check engine warning, sudden loss of power, or the car slowing hard on a hill.
issues.why: Hyundai issued bulletins for hidden fault codes in the hybrid control unit and DC converter on 2019-2021 hybrids, fixed by a software update, and for traction motor fault codes.
issues.next: Have the codes read at a Hyundai dealer and ask about the hybrid control unit software update.

issues.t: High-voltage battery precharge fault code
issues.sym: A hybrid warning light and code P1B77; the car may not go into Ready mode.
issues.why: The battery management software could log a precharge fault. Hyundai released a service campaign with updated software.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the battery management software campaign was done.

issues.t: Electric water pump leak or overheating
issues.sym: Coolant loss, overheating warnings, or warning lights; some owners report the car shutting down.
issues.why: Hyundai ran a service campaign to inspect the electric water pump assembly, and owners report pumps leaking.
issues.next: Check the coolant level and have the dealer confirm the water pump campaign. Stop driving if the car overheats.

issues.t: Check engine light for coolant temperature code P0128
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0128, with no drivability problem.
issues.why: The engine computer's monitoring logic could set this code. Hyundai issued an ECM software update.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the engine computer update.

issues.t: Blind spot warning system fault
issues.sym: Blind-spot or rear cross-traffic warnings stop working, sometimes with a warning message.
issues.why: Hyundai issued a bulletin for fault codes in the rear bumper radar sensors.
issues.next: Have the radar sensors checked and recalibrated if needed. Keep checking your mirrors in the meantime.

issues.t: Wireless phone charger won't charge
issues.sym: Your phone does not charge on the wireless pad.
issues.why: Hyundai issued a bulletin with a diagnostic procedure for some charging pads not charging.
issues.next: Try removing the phone case. If it still fails, have the pad diagnosed.

issues.t: Condensation inside headlights or taillights
issues.sym: Fog or droplets inside the headlights, taillights or fog lamps.
issues.why: Hyundai issued information bulletins on moisture in vented lamps; light fog can be normal, but pooled water is not.
issues.next: If water collects or stays, have the lamp inspected for a damaged seal or crack.

issues.t: Horn stops working
issues.sym: Pressing the horn does nothing.
issues.why: Owners report horn failures with good fuses; dealers replaced the horn in several cases.
issues.next: Get it fixed promptly, since a working horn is a safety item. Have the horn and wiring tested.

issues.t: Warning light with communication code U1341
issues.sym: A warning light on the dash with code U1341.
issues.why: Hyundai issued a bulletin for 2021-2022 Ioniq plug-in hybrids where a communication issue between control units sets this code, fixed by a software update.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the control unit software update.

issues.t: Remote start through the app doesn't work
issues.sym: Remote start from the MyHyundai app or website fails.
issues.why: Hyundai issued a bulletin for Bluelink remote start failures.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about the Bluelink fix, and check that your subscription is active.
